instruction: For testing purposes, I need to disable JavaScript execution in Chrome. Can you turn off JavaScript in the browser settings?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"profile":{"default_content_settings":{"javascript":1}}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to disable JavaScript in Chrome. The evaluator checks profile.default_content_settings.javascript (1=allow, 2=block). Initial state: 1 (JS enabled). Expected state: 2 (JS disabled). Getter returns 'false' when JS is blocked to match expected 'false'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts JavaScript setting from Chrome preferences file at profile.default_content_settings.javascript
Getter correctly maps Chrome's internal values (1=allow, 2=block) to semantic boolean strings ('true'/'false')
Metric exact_match correctly compares getter result with expected value 'false'
Expected value 'false' correctly represents the disabled state required by the instruction
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to ensure preferences file reflects user changes
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the single requirement (JavaScript disabled)
Data flow is logically sound: reads preference → converts to boolean string → exact comparison
